## Frequently Asked Questions

What is K2 and where is it located?

K2 is the world's second-highest mountain at 8,611 metres (28,251 ft), located on the border between Pakistan's Gilgit-Baltistan region and China's Xinjiang province in the Karakoram Range. Its coordinates are 35.8808° N, 76.5133° E. K2 is also known as Chhogori (great mountain in Balti), Mount Godwin-Austen (after the British surveyor who first mapped it in detail), and the Savage Mountain, a phrase coined by American climber George Bell after his 1953 expedition when he described it as 'a savage mountain that tries to kill you.'

How many people have summited K2?

As of 2026, approximately 800 to 850 people have successfully summited K2. Total recorded summits from 1954 to 2025 number approximately 964 when including support team members. The mountain was first summited on July 31, 1954 by Italian climbers Achille Compagnoni and Lino Lacedelli via the Abruzzi Spur. For comparison, Everest has been summited over 10,000 times. K2's significantly lower summit count reflects its shorter weather window, more complex logistics, and extreme technical difficulty.

What is the K2 death rate?

K2's overall death rate is approximately 9.5% based on records from 1930 to 2025 (approximately 92 deaths across 964 summits). The death rate was dramatically higher before 2000 — approximately 29% — when modern weather forecasting and oxygen systems were unavailable. In recent seasons (post-2010), the fatality rate has dropped to approximately 5–7% per season. For comparison, Everest's fatality rate is approximately 1–2%. K2's fatality rate is the second-highest among all 8,000-metre peaks, behind Annapurna.

Why is K2 called the Savage Mountain?

K2 is called the Savage Mountain because of a phrase used by American climber George Bell after the failed 1953 American K2 Expedition. Bell described K2 as 'a savage mountain that tries to kill you.' The nickname stuck because it accurately describes K2's combination of extreme technical difficulty, unpredictable Karakoram weather, high fatality rate, and the concentrated danger of the Bottleneck couloir and serac bands above 8,000 m. Unlike Everest, K2 has no straightforward high-altitude walking section it demands technical climbing from Base Camp to summit.

Has K2 ever been climbed in winter?

Yes, but only once. On January 16, 2021, a team of 10 Nepali climbers made the first-ever winter ascent of K2, becoming the last 8,000-metre peak to be climbed in winter. The team was led by Nirmal Purja (also known as Nims Purja) and included Mingma Gyalje Sherpa, Mingma David Sherpa, Mingma Tenzi Sherpa, and six other Sherpa climbers. They summited at 16:58 local time and deliberately held together to summit as a group. K2 in winter is a separate and vastly more dangerous objective than the summer season, temperatures can drop below -60°C and wind speeds can exceed 200 km/h.

Who was the first woman to climb K2?

Wanda Rutkiewicz of Poland was the first woman to summit K2 on June 23, 1986. She did so without supplemental oxygen as part of a French-American expedition. Rutkiewicz was one of the most accomplished female high-altitude climbers of her era. Gerlinde Kaltenbrunner of Austria later became the first woman to climb all 14 eight-thousanders without supplemental oxygen, including K2, which she summited in 2011.

Is K2 harder than Everest?

Yes, K2 is widely considered technically harder and more dangerous than Everest. K2 has a fatality rate of ~9.5% compared to Everest's 1–2%. K2's technical difficulty stems from sustained 45–80 degree slopes on all routes, the notorious Bottleneck couloir at 8,200 m beneath unstable seracs, the Black Pyramid mixed rock-and-ice section at 6,600–7,200 m, and Karakoram weather that is less predictable than the Himalayan patterns that govern Everest. K2 also has a shorter summit window (typically 3–6 weeks vs Everest's two seasons), less commercial infrastructure, and far fewer rescuers available in an emergency. The mountaineering community refers to K2 as 'the mountaineer's mountain' precisely because of these demands.

What does the death zone mean on K2?

The death zone on K2 refers to the altitude above 8,000 metres where oxygen levels are insufficient to sustain human life indefinitely. Above 8,000 m, the atmospheric pressure is approximately one-third of sea level pressure, and even with supplemental oxygen, the body continues to deteriorate. Climbers experience impaired judgement, muscle weakness, hallucinations, and rapid deterioration after 24–48 hours in the death zone. On K2, the death zone begins at 8,000 m and the summit at 8,611 m sits 611 m above it. The Bottleneck at 8,200 m, the Traverse at 8,200–8,400 m, and the summit snowfield all lie within the death zone.

How much does a K2 expedition cost in 2026?

A K2 expedition with Marvel Treks starts from $8,500 per person for our service package. The total all-in budget for a K2 expedition in 2026 typically ranges from $35,000 to $60,000 per climber. This includes the service package, Pakistan climbing permit ($5,000 per person for summer season), rescue bond, environmental fee, liaison officer costs, international flights ($800–$2,500), personal climbing gear ($5,000–$15,000 if purchasing), high-altitude insurance ($2,000–$4,000), summit bonuses (mandatory, typically $2,000–$3,000 cash), and personal expenses. Contact Marvel Treks for a personalised cost breakdown.

What does the K2 climbing permit cost in 2026?

The individual K2 climbing permit issued by the Gilgit-Baltistan Tourism Department costs $5,000 per person for the summer season (April–September) as of 2025–2026 regulations. Previously, permits were issued collectively at $12,000 for a group of seven (approximately $1,714 per person), but regulations changed to individual permits in 2024–2025. Additional mandatory costs include a $10,000 rescue bond per team (fully refundable) and a $68 environmental fee per climber. Marvel Treks handles all permit applications and submissions on behalf of participants.

How long does a K2 expedition take?

K2 expedition takes 52 to 60 days from arrival in Islamabad to final departure. Marvel Treks' service package covers 40 days of structured itinerary. The timeline includes 2–3 days in Islamabad (briefings, equipment checks), 1 day flying to Skardu, 1 day driving to Askole, 6 days trekking to Base Camp, approximately 30 days of acclimatization rotations and weather waiting at Base Camp and high camps, 1–2 days for the summit push, and 6 days returning to Skardu. Weather delays frequently extend the schedule by 1–2 weeks. Budget for a maximum of 65 days.

What experience do I need to climb K2?

Climbers should have summited at least one 7,000-metre peak and ideally have experience on an 8,000-metre mountain. Required skills include ice climbing ability (WI3–WI4 minimum), crampon technique on slopes above 50 degrees, proficiency with fixed rope ascenders and descenders, experience in multi-week remote expeditions, and comfort using supplemental oxygen. Ideal prerequisite peaks include Broad Peak (8,051 m), Gasherbrum II (8,035 m), or Manaslu (8,163 m). K2 is not appropriate as a first 8,000-metre objective. Marvel Treks conducts a pre-expedition assessment of all applicants.

Do I need supplemental oxygen to climb K2?

Yes, virtually all climbers require supplemental oxygen above Camp 3 (7,800 m) and on summit day. Marvel Treks provides three 4-litre oxygen bottles per climber for use above Camp 3, along with masks and regulators. Some elite high-altitude climbers have summited K2 without supplemental oxygen (notably Gerlinde Kaltenbrunner in 2011), but this is an extreme undertaking reserved for athletes with exceptional altitude physiology and extensive no-oxygen 8,000-metre experience. For the vast majority of climbers, oxygen significantly reduces fatality risk on summit day.

What is the best time to climb K2?

The best and only practical time to climb K2 is late June to early August. During this window, the jet stream shifts north of the Karakoram, wind speeds drop to manageable levels at the summit, and a brief summer window opens. July is the prime month, with most successful K2 summits occurring between July 10 and August 5. Marvel Treks runs all K2 expeditions with late June departures to maximise time in this window. Shoulder seasons (May, late August) are unsuitable. Winter ascents are only for elite specialists.

What visa do I need to climb K2?

All foreign nationals require a Pakistan mountaineering visa, separate from a standard tourist visa. The mountaineering visa is applied for through the Pakistani embassy or consulate in your home country and requires your expedition permit number, a letter from your expedition operator, and medical insurance documentation. Processing typically takes 2–4 weeks. Marvel Treks provides all necessary invitation and expedition documentation to support your visa application. The visa itself typically costs $100–$150 depending on nationality.

What insurance is required for a K2 expedition?

High-altitude rescue and medical evacuation insurance is mandatory for all K2 expedition participants. The minimum requirement is $100,000 in emergency medical evacuation coverage including helicopter rescue from Gilgit-Baltistan. Marvel Treks strongly recommends policies that include: helicopter rescue from altitude, repatriation of remains, trip cancellation, medical treatment, and personal accident coverage. Recommended providers for high-altitude mountaineering insurance include Global Rescue, Ripcord, BMC Travel Insurance (UK), and specialist alpine insurers. Confirm that your policy specifically covers climbing at altitudes above 8,000 m standard travel insurance does not.

What is the Bottleneck on K2?

The Bottleneck is a narrow couloir on the Abruzzi Spur at approximately 8,200 m, directly beneath a large serac band known as the Serac Band. It is the most dangerous single feature on K2's standard route. The couloir is approximately 200 m long, angled at 40–50 degrees, and must be traversed by all climbers attempting the summit via the Abruzzi Spur. The hanging seracs above can and do collapse without warning, releasing ice avalanches directly through the Bottleneck. Climbers minimise risk by passing through the Bottleneck before sunrise, typically between 03:00 and 06:00 on summit day, when cold temperatures reduce serac instability. The 2008 K2 disaster, in which 11 climbers died in one event, was primarily caused by serac collapse in the Bottleneck.

What is House's Chimney on K2?

House's Chimney is a near-vertical rock crack on the Abruzzi Spur at approximately 6,350–6,400 m. It was first climbed by American climber William Houseman (known as Bill House) during the 1938 American K2 Expedition led by Charles Houston. The chimney requires genuine technical rock climbing ability at high altitude typically rated around 5.7 in the Yosemite Decimal System under ideal conditions but significantly harder in crampons, gloves, and at altitude. Fixed ropes are normally placed through House's Chimney during the season.

What is the Black Pyramid on K2?

The Black Pyramid is a 400–600 m section of mixed rock and ice on the Abruzzi Spur between approximately 6,600 m and 7,200 m. It is the most sustained technical section of the Abruzzi Route below the Shoulder and involves steep rock bands, ice fields, and potentially loose rock. The Black Pyramid requires solid crampon technique, ice tool placements, and efficient movement on fixed ropes. Above the Black Pyramid, climbers reach the Shoulder at 7,700–7,800 m where Camp 4 is typically established.

How many camps are on the K2 Abruzzi Route?

The Abruzzi Spur has four established high camps in addition to Base Camp. Base Camp sits at 5,100 m on the Godwin-Austen Glacier. Camp 1 is at approximately 6,050 m above the initial icefall. Camp 2 is at approximately 6,700 m below the Black Pyramid. Camp 3 sits at approximately 7,800 m on or near the Shoulder. Camp 4, the final high camp, is established at approximately 8,300 m just below the Bottleneck. From Camp 4, summit day begins before midnight with an 8–14 hour round trip to the summit and back.

How dangerous is the Baltoro Glacier approach to K2?

The Baltoro Glacier approach from Askole to K2 Base Camp is a 6-day trek at relatively moderate altitude (1,700 m to 5,100 m) and is not technically dangerous for acclimatised trekkers. The trail crosses moraine terrain and glacier ice, with some route-finding required in poor visibility. The primary risks are altitude sickness above 4,000 m, rockfall in narrow valleys near Concordia, and extreme weather exposure. Marvel Treks provides experienced trekking Sherpas and porters for all load-carrying on the approach. The trek itself passes through some of the most dramatic mountain scenery on Earth — Concordia is known as the Throne Room of the Mountain Gods for its views of K2, Broad Peak, Gasherbrum IV, and Mitre Peak.

Can I combine K2 with another Pakistan 8,000-metre peak?

Yes, many climbers combine K2 with Broad Peak (8,051 m) or Gasherbrum I and II (8,068 m / 8,035 m) in the same season, as all these peaks share the Baltoro Glacier approach. Marvel Treks offers combined expedition packages. Note that Pakistan's 2024–2026 permit regulations require a separate individual permit for each peak, so combining two 8,000-metre peaks significantly increases permit costs. Broad Peak is the most common K2 warm-up objective as it shares Base Camp infrastructure and its less technical summit provides excellent acclimatization above 8,000 m.

What is Concordia and why is it significant?

Concordia is the confluence point of the Baltoro and Godwin-Austen glaciers at approximately 4,600 m, reached on day 9 of the K2 approach. From Concordia, climbers have unobstructed views of four of the world's five highest peaks outside of the Himalayan massif, K2 (8,611 m), Broad Peak (8,051 m), Gasherbrum IV (7,925 m), and Gasherbrum I (8,068 m). The camping site at Concordia is one of the most extraordinary mountain settings on Earth and is often called the Throne Room of the Mountain Gods. From Concordia, K2 Base Camp is an additional 6–7 hours' walk up the Godwin-Austen Glacier.

What is Askole and why do expeditions start there?

Askole is a small village in Shigar Valley, Gilgit-Baltistan, at approximately 3,000 m, and is the last permanent human settlement before the Karakoram wilderness. All K2 and Baltoro-area expeditions begin their mountain approach at Askole. The drive from Skardu to Askole takes 6–7 hours on a rough jeep track through the Braldu River valley. At Askole, expedition teams hire local porters who carry loads through the restricted zone into the Baltoro Glacier region. The restricted zone begins at Askole and covers the entire Baltoro, including K2, Broad Peak, and the Gasherbrums.

K2 Expedition registration is now open. Climbing K2 is considered one of the top mountaineering expeditions in the world. The mighty K2 is every tough mountaineer’s dream. We are offering K2 Expedition departures (guided and non-guided) for mountaineers and alpinists from around the world.

Including our **K2 Expedition**, we offer [7,000 to 8,000m expeditions](https://www.apricottours.pk/tour-tag/7000m-peaks-pakistan/) and the following 8,000m plus expeditions given in the table below.

### K2 Climbing Route – Joint K2 Expedition 2025

### Highlights – K2 Expedition

- Highlights

- Very **competitive prices** for an eight thousander peak
- **Field office** and **permanent staff** for logistical arrangements to and from the mountain
- Itinerary based on our mountain guide's **indigenous knowledge** and **vast experience**
- Spectacular **mountain vistas** during the expedition
- Apricot Tours is a fully licensed **native adventure company**
- **Fixed departures** are normally guided by our Pakistani High Altitude Climber(s) (HAC)
- **Private groups** are always one of our top priorities
- We cater to both **guided expeditions** and non-guided **(alpine style)** climbing
- We cater to both **"base camp services"** and **"full board services"**
- **Nepalese Sherpas** available upon timely request (at least 6 months prior to arrival in Pakistan)
- The following **High Altitude Support** available at extra cost
  a. **Pakistani High Altitude Porter** (HAP) - Will carry 20 kg of personal equipment between camps
  b. **Nepalese Private Sherpa** (personal guide/porter) – Carries up to 20 kg (44lbs) of your personal equipment, climbs with you, melts water, cooks, and will be with you every step of the way.
  c. **Personal equipment carriage** service – Sherpa carries up to 10kg (22lbs) of personal equipment up and down the mountain between camps

### Itinerary

Day 01: Arrive at Islamabad International Airport, Islamabad

#### **On this Day**

**GPS Data**
Altitude: 540 m

Our guide(s) will receive you from the airport. Soon you will be transferred to hotels. On this day, our participants can relax and recover from their long journey.

**Pickup information**
It is very easy to spot our guide, holding orange placards with our company’s logo and your name on it. You must arrive at Islamabad International Airport, Islamabad. International flights normally arrive at midnight or in the afternoon. You must give us the details of your flights, both inbound and outbound at least five days prior to your arrival in Pakistan. Our staff/guide will receive you at the gates of international arrivals unless you are taking a connecting flight from another city of Pakistan. The guide/staff will transfer you to our partner hotel. In case you do not require airport transfer, please inform us in advance.

After lunch and some rest at the hotel (ideally if you are arriving in the morning between 9am to 12pm), our guide/representative will pickup all our guests around 6pm for briefing and remaining payments at our office followed by a dinner.

| Accommodation | Twin-sharing room at Chateau Royale [(see pictures)](https://www.apricottours.pk/hotel/chateau-royale-islamabad/), Prestige Residence [(see pictures)](https://www.apricottours.pk/hotel/prestige-residence-islamabad/) or equivalent standard partner hotel (depends on occupancy) in Islamabad. |
| --- | --- |
| Meals | Breakfast, lunch and dinner + tea/coffee and snacks |

Day 02: Free day in Islamabad

#### **On this Day**

**GPS Data**
Altitude: 540 m

On this day we will have have briefing from the Department of Tourism regarding the K2 Expedition in Islamabad before travelling to Skardu.

After briefing we will spend time exploring Islamabad and we will have a taste of tradition Pakistani Food.

| Accommodation | Twin-sharing room at Chateau Royale [(see pictures)](https://www.apricottours.pk/hotel/chateau-royale-islamabad/), Prestige Residence [(see pictures)](https://www.apricottours.pk/hotel/prestige-residence-islamabad/) or equivalent standard partner hotel (depends on occupancy) in Islamabad. |
| --- | --- |
| Meals | Breakfast, lunch and dinner + tea/coffee and snacks |

Day 03: Fly to Skardu, Karakoram

#### **On this Day**

**GPS Data**
Altitude: 2,498 m

Participants on this morning will take the spectacular flight from Islamabad airport to Skardu airport. You will be able to see Nanga Parbat if clouds allow. After arrival in Skardu, the day is free. The participants can shop around and spend some time in peaceful valley. It will be a treat before going on to the K2 Expedition.

| Accommodation | Twin-sharing room at Concordia Motel [(see pictures)](https://www.apricottours.pk/hotel/concordia-motel-skardu/), Mountain Lodge [(see pictures)](https://www.apricottours.pk/hotel/mountain-lodge-hotel-skardu/%20) or equivalent standard partner hotel (depends on occupancy) in Skardu. |
| --- | --- |
| Meals | Breakfast, lunch and dinner + tea/coffee and snacks |

Day 04: Spend free day in Skardu

#### **On this Day**

**GPS Data**
Altitude: 2,498 m

After breakfast, the participants will walk to Kharpocho fort in Skardu, which is located up on a mountain. The Kharpocho fort gives a splendid view of the Indus and Skardu town. The participants will also have an option to take a tour to Sadpara Lake followed by free shopping time in Skardu Bazaar.

During sightseeing, our staff will take care of further government documentation required in Skardu. This can sometimes take two days. We have contingency days towards the end of the trek incase of any delays.

| Accommodation | Twin-sharing room at Concordia Motel [(see pictures)](https://www.apricottours.pk/hotel/concordia-motel-skardu/), Mountain Lodge [(see pictures)](https://www.apricottours.pk/hotel/mountain-lodge-hotel-skardu/%20) or equivalent standard partner hotel (depends on occupancy) in Skardu. |
| --- | --- |
| Meals | Breakfast, lunch and dinner + tea/coffee and snacks |

Day 05: Drive to Askole village

#### On this Day

**GPS Data**
Altitude: 3,015 m

On this day the K2 Expedition will officially kick off as we make our way to the Baltoro Region. The participants will begin the jeep safari towards Daso, the passage will go through the Shigar valley. The journey will be followed on the sides of Braldu river which extends to Askole. Askole will be the last village on our route; the participants will start walking after leaving jeeps behind. However at times the participants may begin their walk before arrival in Askole but it depends on the road conditions. Overall it will take you between six hours to eight hours in covering the distance.

| Accommodation | Camping in twin-sharing dome tent [(see pictures)](https://www.apricottours.pk/hotel/dome-tent/) |
| --- | --- |
| Meals | Breakfast, lunch and dinner + snacks (dry fruit/chocolate) for trek, appetizer (soup/fried-snacks) before dinner and dessert/fruits after dinner |

Day 06: Trek from Askole to Jhola via the snout of Biafo Glacier

#### **On this Day**

**GPS Data**
Altitude: 3,103 m
Distance: 20 km
Time: 5-8 hours

After completion of necessary supplies list and equipment the porters will load up for the trek ahead to Jhola. The valley is gateway to Biafo glacier that flow over fifty kms from Hispar La to Braldu. The participants will experience the moraine walking as the snout of the glacier is crossed and they will descend to lunch spot beside the Korofon river.

The route will take us the confluence of rivers of Braldu and Domordo. The former trail is not taken for the trek and instead a newer trail will lead us to go upstream where the participants will cross the river by bridge. On the other side of the bridge the participants will descend to the edge of Braldu river and will follow the river bank to reach the camp at Jhola.

| Accommodation | Camping in twin-sharing dome tent [(see pictures)](https://www.apricottours.pk/hotel/dome-tent/) |
| --- | --- |
| Meals | Breakfast, lunch and dinner + snacks (dry fruit/chocolate) for trek, appetizer (soup/fried-snacks) before dinner and dessert/fruits after dinner |

Day 07: Trek from Jhola to Paiju following the Braldu river

#### **On this Day**

**GPS Data**
Altitude: 3,418 m
Distance: 19.8 km
Time: 6-7 hours

On this day of our K2 Expedition the participants will follow the Braldu gorge, along the bank of Braldu river. The participants will be able to view astonishing rocks of Trango Tower and Cathedral Peak. The participants should prevent themselves from possible sun burns and during this day as the walking conditions can be very dry and hot.

Several streams from glacier flow down into the valley and on the way the participants will have to use river crossing shoes depending on the water levels. The participants will be able to spot the snout of Baltoro Glacier on a clear day. On this day the participants will end their day by climbing away from the river to camp at Paiju, the last camp where you will see trees until for a while.

| Accommodation | Camping in twin-sharing dome tent [(see pictures)](https://www.apricottours.pk/hotel/dome-tent/) |
| --- | --- |
| Meals | Breakfast, lunch and dinner + snacks (dry fruit/chocolate) for trek, appetizer (soup/fried-snacks) before dinner and dessert/fruits after dinner |

Day 08: Acclimatize and rest in Paiju

#### **On this Day**

**GPS Data**
Altitude: 3,418 m

The participants will spend the day at Paiju Camp for acclimatization and rest. However the porters will take their time to bake themselves bread for next week on the glacier. Acclimatization walk can also be taken towards Paiju Peak base camp on this day. This will be very helpful for the participants before the K2 Expedition as their bodies will acclimatize with the region.

| Accommodation | Camping in twin-sharing dome tent [(see pictures)](https://www.apricottours.pk/hotel/dome-tent/) |
| --- | --- |
| Meals | Breakfast, lunch and dinner + snacks (dry fruit/chocolate) for trek, appetizer (soup/fried-snacks) before dinner and dessert/fruits after dinner |

Day 09: Trek from Paiju to Khoburtse

#### **On this Day**

**GPS Data**
Altitude: 3,788 m
Distance: 14.7 km
Time: 5-7 hours

On this day of the K2 Expedition the walking will get tough however the scenery will become amazing with each step taken onto the snout of Baltoro Glacier. The trail has continuous up and down climbs on the glacial moraine, although the trail is quite safe but it is highly recommended to be careful at all times. The participants will experience the stunning views as they move ahead; the views of Trango Tower and Uli Biaho. The participants are required to go across the glacier to Liligo. From this point the participants will follow a rocky trail which is along the edge of the Baltoro or sometimes to Khoburtse, the side of the glacier where camp will be made.

| Accommodation | Camping in twin-sharing dome tent [(see pictures)](https://www.apricottours.pk/hotel/dome-tent/) |
| --- | --- |
| Meals | Breakfast, lunch and dinner + snacks (dry fruit/chocolate) for trek, appetizer (soup/fried-snacks) before dinner and dessert/fruits after dinner |

Day 10: Cross small glaciers and walk to Urdukus

#### **On this Day**

**GPS Data**
Altitude: 3,905 m
Distance: 6.4 km
Time: 4-6 hours

On this day of the K2 Expedition Trango Towers can be eventually seen after coming across two small glaciers. For the following night the participants will make their stop at Urdukas near the army camp. The camp is 100m above the glacier.

| Accommodation | Camping in twin-sharing dome tent [(see pictures)](https://www.apricottours.pk/hotel/dome-tent/) |
| --- | --- |
| Meals | Breakfast, lunch and dinner + snacks (dry fruit/chocolate) for trek, appetizer (soup/fried-snacks) before dinner and dessert/fruits after dinner |

Day 11: Trek to Goro II, the junction of the Baltoro glaciers and Young husband

#### **On this Day**

**GPS Data**
Altitude: 4,285 m
Distance: 11.9 km
Time: 6-8 hours

On this day of K2 Expedition, the participants will be walking in the middle of the glacier. The medial moraine will be followed, to the south we will get the views of Masherbrum (7821m). The participants will be climbing up and down on the rocky moraine and as the participants move ahead they will walk pass massive ice seracs.

This will be the first night stay camp on Baltoro Glacier at Goro II, it is the confluence of Baltoro Glacier and Younghusband. The temperature may drop dramatically. Masherbrum and Muztagh Tower will be uncovered for the sight.

| Accommodation | Camping in twin-sharing dome tent [(see pictures)](https://www.apricottours.pk/hotel/dome-tent/) |
| --- | --- |
| Meals | Breakfast, lunch and dinner + snacks (dry fruit/chocolate) for trek, appetizer (soup/fried-snacks) before dinner and dessert/fruits after dinner |

Day 12: Trek to Concordia through a rocky moraine

#### **On this Day**

**GPS Data**
Altitude: 4,512 m
Distance: 11.7 km
Time: 5-7 hours

On this day of the K2 Expedition, the participants will reach Concordia after continuously walking up the moraine, on the way more and more high snowcapped peaks will appear, the culmination for the sighting of K2 will be experienced on this day. Other peaks that can be seen include Broad Peak, Mitre Peak, Gasherbrum, Sia Kangri and many more.

| Accommodation | Camping in twin-sharing dome tent [(see pictures)](https://www.apricottours.pk/hotel/dome-tent/) |
| --- | --- |
| Meals | Breakfast, lunch and dinner + snacks (dry fruit/chocolate) for trek, appetizer (soup/fried-snacks) before dinner and dessert/fruits after dinner |

Day 13: Trek to K2 Base Camp

#### **On this Day**

**GPS Data**
GPS Data
Altitude: (5,155m)
Distance: 10 km
Time: 6 hours

Today there is the opportunity to walk up the Godwin-Austen glacier just before the K2 Base camp. We will leave early morning, crossing the glaciers onto the faint trail heading towards K2 (there is a faint rocky trail all the way). As we follow the glacier towards K2 the mountain seems to grow bigger and bigger. Broad Peak rears up to our right and after about 3 hours we pass Broad Peak base camp. We usually have our lunch break here and as we continue carry on with K2 towering above us as we get closer and closer.

Just before base camp, amongst the boulder and ice strewn landscape is the Art Gilkey Memorial. A short scramble brings us to the place where those whose life K2 claimed are remembered. Plaques and engraved tin plates are attached to a small rocky outcrop at the foot of this great mountain. There are great views directly above us of K2. We will camp here for the night.

| Accommodation | Camping in twin-sharing dome tent [(see pictures)](https://www.apricottours.pk/hotel/dome-tent/) |
| --- | --- |
| Meals | Breakfast, lunch and dinner + snacks (dry fruit/chocolate) for trek, appetizer (soup/fried-snacks) before dinner and dessert/fruits after dinner |

Day 14 - 43: Ascent of K2

#### **On this Day**

**GPS Data**
Altitude: 5,150 m
Distance: 8.08 km
Time: 4 weeks

We will start our ascend to the mountain on this day and continue our climb during the four weeks duration. We will have contingency days for better weather windows. Apricot Tours Team will set up the base camp for the K2 Expedition and will continue to assist the expedition during the time frame.

| Accommodation | Camping in twin-sharing dome tent [(see pictures)](https://www.apricottours.pk/hotel/dome-tent/) |
| --- | --- |
| Meals | Breakfast, lunch and dinner + snacks (dry fruit/chocolate) for trek, appetizer (soup/fried-snacks) before dinner and dessert/fruits after dinner |

Day 44: Trek back to Concordia and rest

#### **On this Day**

**GPS Data**
Altitude: 4,512 m
Distance: 11.7 km
Time: 5-7 hours

On this day, we retrace our steps back to Concordia after the successful K2 Expedition.

| Accommodation | Camping in twin-sharing dome tent [(see pictures)](https://www.apricottours.pk/hotel/dome-tent/) |
| --- | --- |
| Meals | Breakfast, lunch and dinner + snacks (dry fruit/chocolate) for trek, appetizer (soup/fried-snacks) before dinner and dessert/fruits after dinner |

Day 45: Trek to Ali Camp

#### **On this Day**

**GPS Data**
Altitude: 4,500 m
Distance: 14.7 km
Time: 5-6 hours

The participants will set out on slightly different and less explored route. Short detours will be made to avoid crevasses and the participants should walk on rugged ice rather than slippery ice. In case of snow, the participants and the porters will walk together wearing crampons for safety hooked with rope to each other.

The base will be set in Ali camp, where the participants will reach after hiking for 5-6 hours. “Ali Camp” is name after a local porter, who was the first person to cross Gondogoro La Pass.

| Accommodation | Camping in twin-sharing dome tent [(see pictures)](https://www.apricottours.pk/hotel/dome-tent/) |
| --- | --- |
| Meals | Breakfast, lunch and dinner + snacks (dry fruit/chocolate) for trek, appetizer (soup/fried-snacks) before dinner and dessert/fruits after dinner |

Day 46: Trek to Khuispang over Gondogoro La

#### **On this Day**

**GPS Data**
Altitude: 5,585 m
Distance: 19.8 km
Time: 5-7 hours

On this day the participants will wake up as early as 2 am. After gearing up and having breakfast the participants roped as one uni will depart for the Gondogoro La base. Depending upon the situation our support crew will be there to fix ropes or helping the members out with the gears. It takes about 3 hours to get to the top of Gondogoro La Pass. You get to see and experience a breathtaking of all four 8000ers in the baltoro region. (K2, G1, Broad Peak, G2).

While, descending to the other side, fixed ropes will be utilized to the full extent, and use of crampons is vital for the safety of the members. The members will get the views of the beautiful and sword head shaped Laila Peak (6,096m) and one can also has the views of other trinity peaks.

The members will have to be extra careful while descending and watch out for every step they take to avoid jolting stones on their teams members. Upon descending for the slope, the trails becomes easy and the participants will move on the moraine. The camp will be set up in the junction point of Gondogoro and Trinity Glacier called Khuispang (4,600m)

| Accommodation | Camping in twin-sharing dome tent [(see pictures)](https://www.apricottours.pk/hotel/dome-tent/) |
| --- | --- |
| Meals | Breakfast, lunch and dinner + snacks (dry fruit/chocolate) for trek, appetizer (soup/fried-snacks) before dinner and dessert/fruits after dinner |

Day 47: Trek to Saicho

#### **On this Day**

**GPS Data**
Altitude: 3,350 m
Distance: 20 km trek
Time: 5-7 hours trek

The participants will continue hiking down, Since the hike downwards would be a comparatively easy hike so the climbing equipment i.e. ropes, crampons will be packed while descending. The mountainous and rocky terrain will be taken over the lush green landscapes of Hushe Valley.

After lunch, the participants will continue hiking to the edge of the Gondogoro Glacier, upon reaching the edge they will find a trail which will lead them to the beautiful valley of rhubarb and grass.

At the end of the valley there are 02 different routes to the destination. Our guide with the consent of local porters will decide the trails they are being frequently used.

The trek gets easy when the two trails meet. The members will see the huts made of stones by herders and local settlers. On this day the participants will experience the sign of the settlements in the area and will be able to breathe easily due to big trees and lower altitude. Camp will be setup at Saicho (3,350m), a part of sand with little grass along the flowing glacier water steams.

| Accommodation | Camping in twin-sharing dome tent [(see pictures)](https://www.apricottours.pk/hotel/dome-tent/) |
| --- | --- |
| Meals | Breakfast, lunch and dinner + snacks (dry fruit/chocolate) for trek, appetizer (soup/fried-snacks) before dinner and dessert/fruits after dinner |

Day 48: Trek to Hushe and drive to Skardu Town

#### **On this Day**

**GPS Data**

Altitude: 2,498 m
Distance: 20 km trek + 127 km drive
Time: 5-7 hours trek + 6 hours drive

On this day the participants have to trek down for only 3-4 hours, the river stream of glacier melted water of Charakusa, Ailling, Masherbrum and Gondogoro Glaciers. The participants will start see the signs of residences, shelter, fiels and signs of people living.

The participants will experience the 02 storey shelters of the Hushe village, where the ground floor is for cattles and the first floor is for the family to live. After setting up the camp the participants can explore the beautiful hushe valley and interact with the locals. This would be the last camping day of the Gondogoro La Trek.

Upon reaching Hushe, the participants will depart for Skardu town from Hushe and the journey offers a lot of beautiful scenes of the different small village of the Hushe Valley. The participants will cross a suspension bridge above Shyok River (which flows from Ladakh, India) to get to the other side.

In the past traditional rafts which were made of goat skin fill with air were use to cross the river. The suspension bridge which is use now to cross was built in 1990’s. Upon crossing the bridge, the participants will the reach Khaplu.

The drive from Khaplu to Skardu becomes smooth and the route to be followe is the paved road along the shayok river which leads to the confluence with Indus River. Upon driving along Indus River the Participants will reach Skardu in 4 hours. The participants can have the facilities which they did not have for 02 weeks. The first on that list would be taking a hot shower and secondly having a good meal.

| Accommodation | Twin-sharing room at Concordia Motel [(see pictures)](https://www.apricottours.pk/hotel/concordia-motel-skardu/), Mountain Lodge [(see pictures)](https://www.apricottours.pk/hotel/mountain-lodge-hotel-skardu/%20) or equivalent standard partner hotel (depends on occupancy) in Skardu. |
| --- | --- |
| Meals | Breakfast, lunch and dinner + tea/coffee and snacks |

Day 49: Debriefing at Skardu

#### **On this Day**

**GPS Data**

Altitude: 2,288 m

On this day the participants will have debriefing from the Department of Tourism after the completion of the K2 Expedition.

After the debriefing the participants can rest and have a peaceful time around the valley.

| Accommodation | Twin-sharing room at Concordia Motel [(see pictures)](https://www.apricottours.pk/hotel/concordia-motel-skardu/), Mountain Lodge [(see pictures)](https://www.apricottours.pk/hotel/mountain-lodge-hotel-skardu/%20) or equivalent standard partner hotel (depends on occupancy) in Skardu. |
| --- | --- |
| Meals | Breakfast, lunch and dinner + tea/coffee and snacks |

Day 50: Fly to Islamabad

#### **On this Day**

**GPS Data**
Altitude: 538 m

On this day the participants will take a flight from the airport in Skardu to Islamabad aiport. You will have a good time to relax at the hotel in Islamabad.

The domestic flights sometime get cancelled due to weather conditions. Incase of flight cancellation, you will drive to Chilas for overnight. It takes eight to ten hours by a vehicle.

| Meals | Breakfast, lunch and dinner + tea/coffee and snacks |

This day is allocated for any potential delays in case the domestic flight does not operate the previous day. Our guests will depart early morning from Chilas to Islamabad which can take up to ten hours. However it will be a free day in case the participants make it to Islamabad on the domestic flight. This time can be utilized to sign the final paper work and sightseeing.

Day 52: Fly to home country

#### **On this Day**

Meals included: Breakfast

Our staff will transfer all our guests to the airport on their respective departure timings. The checkout time of all our partner hotels is 12pm.

- Important Notes

#### **Why should you register very early?**

**\1. Team building:** It takes time to formulate a good team. We go through all incoming applications and formulate the best team of mountaineers (on the basis of experience). Although our vet process is not very strict, our top priority is always the safety of fellow climbers. We will not accept all applications only to maximize the number of the mountaineers.

**\2. Logistics:** Our climbing adventures involve a lot of logistics. This includes reserving/assigning high altitude porters, guides and other staff in advance. It also involves a lot of procurement (equipment, food etc). This is not possible during the last hours. During winters expeditions, most of the supplies are transported to base camps two to three months prior to the expedition because winters in the mountains of Pakistan are very harsh and it becomes almost impossible to for porters to walk through the trail with heavy supplies.

**\3. Climbing Permit:** Pakistani government tourism laws require tour operators to submit applications for climbing (along with all documents e.g. passport copies, photos, etc) at least **55 days** prior to arrival in Pakistan.

**4.Domestic Flights:** We might not be able to get you on the domestic flight to Skardu if you do not pay your deposit on time. Domestic flight seats are sold very fast way ahead of time because there are only two flights to Skardu during peak season. This is a very serious concern.

**CANCELLATION AND REFUND POLICIES**

#### **Cancellation Policies**

**By the Joint Expedition Team:**
If the minimum requirement of 6 participants not be met by April 30, 2025, deposits will be refunded within 7 days, subject to the deduction of transfer fees and based on the prevailing exchange rate at the time of the refund.

**By Participants/Clients:**

1. Deposits are non-refundable.
2. Participants are advised to take out third-party travel cancellation Insurance. Personal travel insurance (Recommendation/Rescue Partners: [Global Rescue](https://ss.globalrescue.com/#/signup/step1?rp=ApricotTours&_gl=1*1qutt5u*_gcl_au*NzQ0MjMwMDMxLjE3NDY1NDQ3OTQuNzk4MjcyMDUzLjE3NDc0MDAzMjMuMTc0NzQwMDMyMw..*_ga*NTgxNDIzMDg4LjE3MTc2ODM2MzE.*_ga_Q05C49SZSQ*czE3NDkwMjYwOTgkbzI5JGcxJHQxNzQ5MDI2MTE5JGozOSRsMCRoMA..&package=1110294))

#### **Cancellation Charges**

- Deposits are non-refundable and non-transferable.
- Cancellations made **16 to 50 days** prior to departure incur a 70% loss of the total trip cost.
- Cancellations made **15 days or less** before departure incur a 100% loss of the total trip cost.

**Refund Requests after cancellations from the client (for balance payments)**

- All refund requests must be made in writing and received within the periods stated above.

#### Currency

All international climbers are charged in US Dollars (USD) or equivalent in GBP or EUR.

#### Other Notes

- Due to the nature and heavy costs of government and operator permits, Apricot Tours must follow a precise refund policy.
- Participants that choose to leave an active expedition for any reason are not entitled to any refunds
- Apricot Tours highly recommends trip cancellation insurance for all expeditions

### Overview – K2 Expedition

The route to K2 goes through the famous Shigar Valley and Baltoro Glacier region of Baltistan. There are several high peaks, which are situated in this world’s largest temperate zone glacier. Only the highest or more prominent ones have been named or climbed. An incredible nineteen of these peaks in the Baltoro region tower over 7,600m while four of them are 8000ers.

As we know K2 to be the 2nd highest mountain on the planet but the “Savage Mountain” is the king in the mountain realm. Among the 8000 peaks. It is a very strenuous and tough climb. It is 10x less climbed and highly technical compared to the Mount Everest. Only those who dare to conquer the Savage Mountain will be remembered in the books of history.

The first route ever taken for the K2 Expedition was attempted via the Abruzzi Ridge or the Standard Route. This is most used route for the K2 Expedition via the Abruzzi Spur (Southeast Ridge) although there are other routes to climb but this one is sound and has higher chances of the ascent. In 1909, K2 Expedition was first attempted by Luigi Amedeo, Duke of the Abruzzi but was its first successful K2 Expedition was completed by an Italian Team on July 31, 1954. The K2 Expedition was led by Ardito Desio and the two climbers who actually reached the top were Lino Lacedelli and Achille Compagnoni.

We will use the Aburuzzi Route for our ascend. This spur begins at an altitude of 5,400 m/17,700 ft, where Advanced Base Camp is usually placed. The route follows an alternating series of ice fields, rock ribs, snow slopes and some technical rock climbing on two famous features, “House’s Chimney” and the “Black Pyramid”.

Above the Black Pyramid, dangerously exposed and difficult to navigate slopes lead to the easily visible “Shoulder”. The last major obstacle is a narrow couloir known as the “Bottleneck”, which places climbers dangerously close to hanging seracs. It was partly due to the collapse of one of these seracs around 2001 that no climber’s summitted the peak in 2002 and 2003 and most of the eleven people lost their lives due to the breaking of huge ice blocks from this cliff and often on their way down.

## K2 Climbing Expedition 2026

Embarking on a K2 Climbing Expedition is a journey that is not for the faint of heart. The world's second tallest peak, K2 is known for its treacherous terrain, extreme weather conditions, and challenging routes that have claimed the lives of many climbers. However, for those who are up for the challenge, the rewards are immeasurable. As a native team, we understand the terrain, the climate, and the culture of the region better than anyone else. Our team consists of experienced and skilled mountaineers who are dedicated to ensuring your safety and success on the mountain.

At the heart of our expedition is our commitment to offering the best cost and services to our clients. We understand that embarking on a K2 Climbing Expedition can be a costly affair, which is why we offer competitive pricing without compromising on the quality of our services. Our team will provide you with expert guidance and support, including logistics, equipment, and provisions necessary for the climb. We are committed to ensuring that your climb is safe, comfortable, and unforgettable. From the moment you arrive in Pakistan to the day you summit K2, we will be with you every step of the way, ensuring that you have the experience of a lifetime. Join us on this journey to conquer one of the most challenging peaks in the world, and we promise that you will come back with memories that will last a lifetime.

## Itinerary

Arrival at Islamabad International Airport. Our staff will welcome the team and transfer members to the hotel. Initial briefing, document verification, and rest after international travel.

**Overnight:** Hotel in Islamabad

Early morning flight to Skardu (subject to weather). Enjoy breathtaking aerial views of Nanga Parbat and the Karakoram Range. On arrival, transfer to hotel.
*If flight is canceled, travel by road via the Karakoram Highway (2 days).*

**Overnight:** Hotel in Skardu

Rest day in Skardu for recovery and acclimatization. Final shopping for fresh supplies, fuel check, porter arrangements, and completion of **K2 climbing expedition permits** and government formalities.

**Overnight:** Hotel in Skardu

Drive by 4x4 jeep along the Indus and Braldu Rivers to Askole, the last settlement before the Karakoram glaciers and the gateway to the **K2 climbing expedition** route.

**Overnight:** Camp at Askole

Start trekking for the **K2 climbing expedition**. Trek along the Braldu River with impressive views of Bakhor Das Peak.

**Trekking Time:** 6–7 hours
**Overnight:** Camp at Jhola

A scenic trek with gradual ascent. The dramatic granite spires of Trango Towers and Cathedral Peaks dominate the skyline.

**Trekking Time:** 6–7 hours
**Overnight:** Camp at Paiju

Rest and acclimatization day. Optional short hike on the Paiju Glacier to prepare the body for Baltoro Glacier trekking.

**Overnight:** Camp at Paiju

Enter the Baltoro Glacier, one of the longest glaciers outside the polar regions, marking a major milestone of the K2 climbing expedition approach.

**Overnight:** Camp at Khoburtse

Trek to Urdukas, one of the most scenic camps of the Baltoro, offering panoramic views of surrounding granite giants.

**Overnight:** Camp at Urdukas

Trek on the central Baltoro Glacier with stunning views of Masherbrum and Gasherbrum IV.

**Overnight:** Camp at Goro II

Trek to Concordia, famously known as the “Throne Room of the Mountain Gods.” Enjoy spectacular views of **K2, Broad Peak, and Gasherbrum I & II**.

**Overnight:** Camp at Concordia

Final trek to **K2 Base Camp**, the operational heart of the **K2 climbing expedition**. Establish base camp and organize equipment.

**Overnight:** Camp at K2 Base Camp

## **Day 13–15: K2 Base Camp – Rest & Acclimatization**

Rest and acclimatization days at base camp. Medical checks, route observation, rope fixing coordination, and acclimatization hikes above base camp.

**Overnight:** K2 Base Camp

This period is dedicated to the core **K2 climbing expedition**, including:

· Load carries between Base Camp, Camp I (6,050m), Camp II (6,700m), and Camp III (7,200m)

· Establishment of high camps and fixing ropes through House Chimney, Black Pyramid, and Shoulder

· Multiple rotations for acclimatization

· Rest days at Base Camp between carries

· Continuous weather monitoring and route safety assessment

Camps are typically established as follows:

· **Camp I:** 6,050m

· **Camp II:** 6,700m

· **Camp III:** 7,200m

· **Camp IV:** 7,800m (Shoulder of K2)

This flexible window ensures climbers are fully acclimatized and ready for a safe summit attempt.

Reserved for summit attempts delayed by weather, second summit window, or additional descent time during the **K2 expedition****.**

Begin trek back after completing the K2 climbing expedition.

**Overnight:** Camp at Concordia

Trek back along the Baltoro Glacier.

**Overnight:** Camp at Goro II

Trek back to Paiju campsite.

**Overnight:** Camp at Paiju

Trek along the Braldu River.

**Overnight:** Camp at Jhola

Final trekking day of the **K2 climbing expedition****.**

**Overnight:** Camp or Guesthouse in Askole

Drive back to Skardu by jeep.

**Overnight:** Hotel in Skardu

Flight to Islamabad (or road journey if required). Farewell dinner and expedition debrief.

**Overnight:** Hotel in Islamabad

Transfer to Islamabad International Airport for final departure.

## Highlights

- Standing on the summit of K2 (8,611m) — the ultimate achievement of the K2 climbing expedition and one of mountaineering’s greatest challenges.
- Climbing the legendary Abruzzi Spur, the most iconic and technical route in high-altitude mountaineering history.
- Operating from K2 Base Camp at Concordia, surrounded by four 8000-meter peaks in the heart of the Karakoram.
- Highly competitive pricing for one of the world’s most technical and demanding eight-thousand-meter peaks.
- Permanent field office and experienced logistics team ensuring smooth operations from arrival to departure.

# Overview

K2 or Mount Godwin-Austen, also known as Chogho Ree among the locals and Savage Mountain among foreign climbers, is the second-highest mountain peak in the world after Mount Everest, with a height of 8611 meters from the sea level. This grand peak is situated on the border of China and Pakistan in the Karakoram Range. The first successful summit of K2 was made in 1954 by Lino Lacedelli and Achille Campagnoni who belonged to an Italian team led by Ardito Desio. According to Wikipedia, overall, 377 people had summited K2 till February 2021. If we compare K2 with Mount Everest, K2 is relatively harder to summit than Mount Everest because of its technical difficulties hard challenges and risk factors. That�s why, K2 has climbed less frequently than Mount Everest. K2 has routes from Pakistan as well as from China. Typically, the most commonly used routes to summit K2 are the Abruzzi Spur from the Pakistani side and the North Ridge on the Chinese side. Climbers often prefer the summer season to summit K2 when weather conditions are relatively more stable than that of winter. Overall, it takes about 50 days from Islamabad, the capital of Pakistan to summit K2 and return. K2 is well known for its harsh weather, which changes rapidly and creates big challenges for climbers. Its steep and technical slope, with high risks of unpredictable avalanches, makes it even harder. The high-altitude environment increases the risk of altitude sickness and frostbite. K2 is considered one of the most difficult peaks to climb. The K2 Expedition is a significant challenge for mountaineers, which requires not only physical power but also strategic planning and thinking capabilities. Despite the risks, the will to conquer this challenging peak continues to attract adventurers from around the world.

## Itinerary

After the member arrives in Islamabad from their places, they will be picked up from the airport by our team and will be transferred to the hotel and allowed to rest and prepare for further travel on the next day.

In the morning flight from Islamabad to Skardu, we will leave. From the flight, we will reach Skardu by noon. In case of cancellation of a flight due to weather conditions or any other reason, we have arrangements to drive by road. We will reach Skardu in the next two days in case of travel by road. Our itinerary will be one day ahead of this case.

A day free for sightseeing in Skardu. We will visit some nearby places in Skardu and will have a glimpse of the beauty of Skardu.

The journey goes alongside the Braldu River in the Shigar Valley. Then, we will start walking towards Askole.

Start trekking towards Jhola. We have to cross the river Braldu by bridge. Jhola is also located near the Braldu River.

A break day for exploring the Paju peak base camp. The team makes the preparations during the day.

Trekking to Liligo starting from the morning, involves beautiful panoramas and landscapes throughout the trek. It also includes a river crossing midway.

day 8 is going to be a tough trekking day as we have to climb and descend the glacial moraines. After crossing the Trango Tower and Uli Biaho, we will reach Urdukas and camp for the night.

Trekking continues again towards Goro II. This time we will be trekking through the glacier. The view of Masherbrum and Muztagh Tower is visible from Goro II.

We will reach Concordia by day 10. From Concordia, we can have a beautiful view of high snowcapped peaks such as Broad Peak, Mitre Peak, Gasherbrum and Sia Kangri as well as the aesthetic view of the Great K2.

We will start our trek in the early morning towards the k2 base camp from Concordia. The way includes a scenic view of sky-touching peaks.

We will start climbing from this day and continue our climb for at least 4 weeks for a distance of about 8.08 km. This specific time includes ascending k2 as well as descending back to base camp. We have included contingency time as well in case of any weather issue or any other time-consuming occurrence. The team of Mountain Tiger Treks and Tours will be assisting throughout the expedition.

After arriving back at the K2 base camp, we will spend a night again here and rest after the great success. A celebration of the success will be given.

After spending a night at K2 Base Camp, our journey moves back to Goro II.

Instead of camping at Urdukas, we will move down the Baltoro Glacier towards Khobursay which will need two hours more. So, our trek will start in the early morning this day.

This day, again instead of camping at Paju, we will trek down to Bardumal. This will take 3 more hours. So we have to start our trek in the early morning.

Starting early in the morning again, we will trek back to Askoli from Bardumal. We will spend this night as the last night of our trekking in Askole.

Early in the morning, we will be coming back to Skardu by using the Jeep service.

The flight typically occurs in the morning. So, we will reach Islamabad by noon on day 19. After reaching Islamabad, you are allowed to take a rest in the hotel.

In case of any flight cancellation due to weather issues or any other issue, we will reach Islamabad this day. Otherwise, we can utilize this day to explore Islamabad. We will be having a farewell dinner in Skardu or Islamabad as well.

All members are free to go to their places. Our staff will transfer you all to the airport.

# The Savage Mountain

8,611m — The world's second-highest and most challenging 8000er. A true test of mountaineering skill and endurance. Since 2012, Pakistan Explorer has been the trusted local partner for K2 expeditions.

8,611m  World Rank: 2  60 Days  Abruzzi Route

Inquire About K2 View Itinerary

## Why Climb K2?

K2 is not just a mountain. It is the ultimate test. The Abruzzi route offers a pure alpine challenge — steep, technical, and relentlessly demanding. Fewer than 400 climbers have summitted. This is the expedition that defines careers.

#### Pure Challenge

No oxygen at 8,000m. Technical rock and ice. The Abruzzi route demands respect. This is not a "tourist" mountain — it's a climber's mountain.

#### Elite Achievement

Only 400+ climbers have summitted K2. You will join one of the most exclusive clubs in mountaineering history.

#### World-Class Setting

The Karakoram offers the world's most dramatic mountain scenery — four 8000ers visible from Concordia. Unforgettable.

#### Full Local Support

Experienced HAPs, licensed guides, and a Liaison Officer ensure safety, compliance, and success. Since 2012, we've been the local partner of choice.

## Overview

K-2 is located at the Northeastern border of Pakistan and its north face is located in the Chinese territory. An estimated eight square kilometers of area around K-2 holds another three 8000ers and more than six dozen 7000ers, and is also home of the longest glaciers on earth after the polar caps. **Gasherbrum 1 (The Hidden Peak), Gasherbrum 2, and Broad Peak** are located adjacent to K-2, which effectively makes it the climbing heaven for mountaineers from all over the world.

K-2 has a unique shape which gives it the typical look of a mountain rather than the flatter and easier to climb Everest. This granite pyramid is consistently steep and stands 3000 meters from the base. It has some of the steepest vertical drops on almost all sides, which makes it all the more difficult to map a route to the top. Since the **first ascent in 1954 by an Italian party**, several routes have been explored to the top of K2 with **Abruzzi (south-south east)** being the most frequent and relatively easier one.

K2 involves mix climbing of all genres and is considered highly technical between all the four high camps. The Abruzzi also throws up phenomenal challenges along the route including **"the House Chimney", "the Black Pyramid"** and the infamous **"Bottleneck"** before the final ascent to the summit at 8,611m.

Pakistan Explorer provides a fully-supported K2 expedition with comprehensive logistics, permits, High Altitude Porters (HAPs), and safety protocols. A serving Pakistan Army Liaison Officer is also attached with the expedition who stays in Base Camp for the entire duration.

### Quick Facts

- Elevation: 8,611 m
- Prominence: 4,020 m
- First Ascent: July 31, 1954
- First Ascenders: Achille Compagnoni, Lino Lacedelli
- Duration: 60 Days
- Ideal Time: Mid June – End August
- Royalty Fee: USD 12,000 (7-member expedition)
- Application: 3 months in advance

[Inquire About K2](https://wa.me/923195285268?text=Hi%20Pakistan%20Explorer%2C%20I%20want%20to%20climb%20K2.)

## The Abruzzi Route Challenges

K2's Abruzzi route presents climbers with some of the most formidable obstacles in mountaineering.

#### House Chimney

A steep, narrow chimney that requires technical climbing skills at high altitude.

#### Black Pyramid

Exposed rock climbing on dark colored granite at extreme altitude.

#### The Bottleneck

The infamous steep couloir with hanging seracs — the most dangerous section of the route.

#### Steep Vertical Drops

Consistently steep terrain from base to summit with some of the steepest vertical drops on any 8000er.

## Expedition Itinerary

60-day expedition — from Islamabad to the summit of K2.

Day 1

#### Arrival in Islamabad

Airport Transfer • Overnight stay in Islamabad (3-star)

Day 2

#### Flight to Skardu

Flight to Skardu (or road via Chilas 24hrs) • Hotel Check-in (3-star)

Day 3

#### Briefing & Preparations

Briefing at Alpine Club of Pakistan • Grocery • Overnight in Hotel

Day 4

#### Skardu to Askoli

4×4 Jeeps • Night in camps • Max Altitude: 3,050m • Duration: 7-8 hours

Day 5

#### Askole to Jhola

Night in camps • Max Altitude: 3,220m • Trek duration: 7-8 hours

Day 6

#### Jhola to Paiyu

Night in camps • Max Altitude: 3,400m • Trek duration: 8-9 hours

Day 7

#### Paiyu to Khoburse

Night in camps • Max Altitude: 3,800m • Trek duration: 8-9 hours

Day 8

#### Khoburse to Goro-1

Night in camps • Max Altitude: 4,200m • Trek duration: 8-9 hours

Day 9

#### Goro-1 to K2 Advance Base Camp

Overnight in tents • Max Altitude: 5,400m • Trek duration: 10-12 hours

Day 10-50

#### Acclimatization & Climbing

Designated 40 days for acclimatization, rotations, and summit push. Camps established at 6,000m, 6,700m, 7,400m, and 8,000m.

Day 51-56

#### Trek Back to Askoli

6 days trekking back via the same route

Day 57

#### Askoli to Skardu

4×4 Jeeps • Night in Hotel (3-star) • Duration: 6-7 hours

Day 58

#### Skardu to Islamabad

De-briefing at Alpine Club • Flight to Islamabad • Overnight stay (3-star)

Day 59-60

#### Fly Out

Departure from Islamabad — end of expedition

[Plan Your K2 Expedition](https://wa.me/923195285268?text=Hi%20Pakistan%20Explorer%2C%20I%20want%20to%20plan%20my%20K2%20expedition.)

## Your K2 Expedition Journey

From your first inquiry to standing on the summit — we handle everything so you can focus on the climb.

1

#### Consultation

Tell us your experience, goals, and timeline. We'll assess feasibility and plan your K2 expedition.

No commitment

2

#### Itinerary & Pricing

Receive a detailed itinerary, transparent pricing, and a breakdown of all costs and inclusions.

Clear & honest

3

#### Permits & Logistics

We handle all paperwork — climbing permits, NOCs, insurance, and coordination with the Alpine Club of Pakistan.

# K2: The Savage Mountain

The world's most challenging summit

Last updated: July 2026 · Reviewed by Javeed Iqbal, Founder

Elevation

8,611m

Difficulty

Extreme

Duration

60 to 70 Days

Best Season

Jun to Aug

## K2 Expedition: a complete guide to climbing K2

K2 is the second-highest mountain on Earth at 8,611 metres, and by almost every measure the hardest of the fourteen 8,000-metre peaks to climb. It sits in the Karakoram on the border between Pakistan and China, at the head of the Baltoro Glacier. Climbers call it the Savage Mountain. For roughly every four people who have reached the summit, one has died on the slopes. That ratio has improved in the modern era but still leaves K2 far deadlier than Everest. A K2 expedition is a 60-to-70-day commitment, and the summit often comes down to a few hours of stable weather as much as to fitness or skill.

### Where is K2?

K2 lies in Gilgit-Baltistan in northern Pakistan, in the Central Karakoram, straddling the frontier with China's Xinjiang. The Pakistani side, reached via the Baltoro Glacier from Skardu, is where the great majority of expeditions take place. The peak rises at the junction of the Baltoro and Godwin-Austen glaciers, ringed by giants: Broad Peak and Gasherbrum I and II are all within sight. There is no road, no village, and no helicopter rescue at altitude. Base Camp sits at about 5,000 metres on the Godwin-Austen Glacier, a week's walk from the last jeep track at Askole.

### How hard is K2, and how dangerous?

K2's summit success rate sits around 25 to 30 percent, against 50 to 65 percent on Everest. Its fatality rate has historically run near 23 to 25 percent, though better forecasting, fixed ropes, and stronger high-altitude support have brought the modern figure down to roughly 12 to 13 percent. Recent counts put about 96 deaths against roughly 800 successful ascents. The reasons are structural. K2 is steeper, more technical, and more exposed than Everest, with no easy line from any side. The weather turns faster, the climbing is harder at every camp, and self-reliance is the rule. No one is coming to carry you down from 8,000 metres.

### K2 vs Everest: why K2 is harder

Everest is higher, but K2 is the harder and more dangerous climb. Everest has fixed lines, ladders over the Khumbu Icefall, large commercial support, and helicopter rescue to the lower camps; in a good season more than half of those who try it reach the top. K2 has none of that safety net above Base Camp. The climbing is steeper and more sustained, the summit day longer and more exposed, and the margin for error far smaller. It is why serious alpinists measure themselves against K2 rather than Everest.

### The Abruzzi Spur route

About three-quarters of all K2 expeditions climb the Abruzzi Spur, the southeast ridge first attempted by Luigi Amedeo, Duke of the Abruzzi, in 1909 and finally climbed by the Italians Achille Compagnoni and Lino Lacedelli in 1954. It is the standard route because it offers the most reliable camp positions and the best route-fixing, not because it is gentle.

From Base Camp the route climbs to Camp 1 at about 6,100m on the lower spur, then through rock buttresses and chimneys to Camp 2 at 6,700m. Camp 3 at around 7,300m sits below the Black Pyramid, a steep mixed rock-and-ice band that is the technical crux of the lower mountain. Camp 4 is pitched on the Shoulder at roughly 7,800m. The summit push tackles the Bottleneck, a narrow ice couloir at about 8,200m running directly beneath a wall of hanging seracs. It is the most dangerous stretch on the mountain, and most teams move through it in the dark, aiming to summit by midday and clear it again before the ice warms.

| Stage | Altitude | What it involves |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Base Camp | 5,150 m | On the Godwin-Austen Glacier, the staging point for the whole climb |
| Camp 1 | about 6,100 m | The lower spur |
| Camp 2 | 6,700 m | Reached through rock buttresses and chimneys |
| Camp 3 | around 7,300 m | Below the Black Pyramid, the technical crux of the lower mountain |
| Camp 4 | roughly 7,800 m | Pitched on the Shoulder |
| The Bottleneck | about 8,200 m | Narrow ice couloir under hanging seracs. The most dangerous stretch, usually crossed in the dark |
| Summit | 8,611 m | Teams aim to top out by midday and re-cross the Bottleneck before the ice warms |

### The Baltoro Glacier approach

Before any climbing begins there is the walk in, and it is one of the great treks on Earth. From Askole the trail follows the Braldu River and then the Baltoro Glacier for about seven days. You pass beneath the Trango Towers, some of the largest granite walls in the world, and the fluted ice of Masherbrum, before reaching Concordia, where the Baltoro meets the Godwin-Austen. Four 8,000-metre peaks stand in view at once from here. From Concordia it is a final day up to K2 Base Camp. The approach doubles as acclimatisation and is, for many climbers, half the reason to come.

### Best time to climb K2

The season is narrow: July and August. In high summer the Karakoram jet stream lifts north and opens the only realistic windows of stable weather. K2 is effectively unclimbable in spring. May, the prime month on Everest, brings deep snow and ferocious wind here. Winter ascents exist but belong to a tiny elite; the first was completed only in January 2021, by a Nepali team led by Nirmal Purja and Mingma Gyalje Sherpa. A full expedition runs 60 to 70 days because climbers need weeks of rotations between camps to acclimatise and then must wait, sometimes a fortnight, for a single safe summit window.

### Acclimatisation, rotations and oxygen

The slow part of a K2 expedition is acclimatisation. After reaching Base Camp, climbers spend several weeks making rotations, climbing to Camp 1, then Camp 2, sleeping high and dropping back down so the body can adapt to thinner air. Each rotation pushes a little higher before a final rest at Base Camp ahead of the summit bid. Most commercial climbers use supplemental oxygen above Camp 3 or Camp 4, along with a personal high-altitude guide; a small minority attempt K2 without bottled oxygen, which sharply raises both the difficulty and the risk. Fixed ropes are placed on the steep sections by a dedicated rope-fixing team early in the season, and the timing of that work often sets the rhythm for everyone on the mountain.

### The dangers: weather, seracs and the death zone

K2's reputation rests on objective hazards that no amount of fitness removes. The seracs above the Bottleneck can collapse without warning. Storms build fast and can pin climbers at high camps for days, with little margin before food, fuel, and strength run out. Above 8,000 metres, in the death zone, the body deteriorates by the hour and clear thinking gets harder. Most accidents happen on the descent, not the summit, when climbers are exhausted and the weather is closing in. A good expedition plans around these realities with conservative turnaround times, careful forecasting, and the discipline to abandon a summit push when the window is not truly open. The mountain will still be there next year; the goal is to be there too.

### Permits, royalty and cost

K2 requires a Pakistan mountaineering permit and a peak royalty paid to Gilgit-Baltistan, along with a liaison officer assigned to the expedition. Permit and royalty costs generally fall between $6,000 and $12,000 per climber and have been in flux: Gilgit-Baltistan moved to sharply raise K2 fees in 2025, the change was challenged in court by Pakistani tour operators, and a compromise structure now applies. A full commercial expedition typically runs from around $18,000 for a base-camp service up to $50,000-$100,000 or more for a fully supported package with oxygen and high-altitude staff, depending on the operator. Pricing on this page is indicative; we quote each expedition individually.

### What it takes to climb K2

K2 is not a first 8,000er. Operators expect a serious record before they will take you, usually a previous 8,000-metre summit, or at least strong experience on 7,000-metre peaks, with confident use of crampons, fixed ropes, and ascenders on steep ground. Beyond the physical, K2 rewards patience and judgement: the willingness to turn around, to wait out weather, and to keep moving through the Bottleneck when stopping would feel easier. Months of endurance and strength training, a structured acclimatisation plan, and the right team are what separate a summit from a long walk back down from Camp 4.

Go With Guide Pakistan runs fully supported K2 expeditions with experienced high-altitude guides, Baltoro approach logistics from Skardu, permit and liaison handling, fixed camps, oxygen, and full base-camp support. For those who want to stand at the foot of the Savage Mountain without climbing it, we also arrange the K2 Base Camp trek.

## Climbing History

1902

First Reconnaissance

Oscar Eckenstein and Aleister Crowley led the first attempt, reaching approximately 6,600m on the Northeast Ridge.

1954

First Summit

Achille Compagnoni and Lino Lacedelli of Italy reached the summit on July 31 via the Abruzzi Spur, completing the first ascent.

1977

Second Ascent

A large Japanese expedition made the second ascent via the Abruzzi Spur, 23 years after the first, a mark of K2's extreme difficulty.

1986

Year of Tragedy and Triumph

13 climbers summited across multiple expeditions, but 13 also died. Wanda Rutkiewicz became the first woman to summit K2.

2004

50th Anniversary

Spanish climber Carlos Soria summited at age 65, while multiple international teams reached the top in favorable conditions.

2021

First Winter Ascent

A Nepali team of 10 climbers led by Nirmal Purja and Mingma Gyalje Sherpa reached the summit on January 16, completing the last 8000m winter ascent.

K2 requires a Pakistan mountaineering permit and a peak royalty paid to Gilgit-Baltistan, along with a liaison officer assigned to the expedition. Permit and royalty costs generally fall between $6,000 and $12,000 per climber and have been in flux: Gilgit-Baltistan moved to sharply raise K2 fees in 2025, the change was challenged in court by Pakistani tour operators, and a compromise structure now applies. A full commercial expedition typically runs from around $18,000 for a base-camp service up to $50,000-$100,000 or more for a fully supported package with oxygen and high-altitude staff, depending on the operator. Pricing on this page is indicative; we quote each expedition individually.

Our estimated cost for a fully supported K2 expedition starts at $55,000 per person, and we quote each expedition individually. Across the market, a commercial expedition typically runs from around $18,000 for a base-camp service up to $50,000-$100,000 or more for a fully supported package with oxygen and high-altitude staff. Part of that is the Pakistan mountaineering permit and the peak royalty paid to Gilgit-Baltistan, which generally fall between $6,000 and $12,000 per climber. Those fees have been in flux: Gilgit-Baltistan moved to sharply raise them in 2025, tour operators challenged the change in court, and a compromise structure now applies. Our price includes the permit and royalty, a liaison officer and base camp staff, all camps, tents and high-altitude equipment, supplemental oxygen and medical supplies, the Baltoro approach logistics and an experienced high-altitude team.
